subject: Vulnerability program: scan rhythm, CVE SLA mapping and evidence packet
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@brightgate-audit.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Murray <alex.murray@aurorapayments.com>
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request - VM evidence & SLA mapping for Aurora Payments SIG review

Hi Priya,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of Aurora Payments' SIG intake we need a compact evidence packet that shows: current authenticated/unauthenticated scan cadence, proof that critical/high CVEs are tracked to remediation timelines, and the SLA matrix you commit to for different severity levels.

Can you provide:
- a single CSV index of the last three months of scans (scanner name, date, scope, top findings)
- your CVE SLA matrix (critical/high/medium/low) and an example ticket showing a triage->remediate timeline (redacted)
- confirmation of cadence for infra vs containers vs third-party deps

Deadline for the SIG packet is EOD PDT on Tuesday (2027-05-11). If you expect any exceptions, flag them now.

Best,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Senior Security Assessor, BrightGate Audit
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@brightgate-audit.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Alex Murray <alex.murray@aurorapayments.com>
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request - VM evidence & SLA mapping for Aurora Payments SIG review

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear list. We can deliver a compact packet that meets the SIG ask. Overview here and I attached the files referenced below.

Quick summary (high level):
- Scan cadence: authenticated agent scans (in-host) run weekly for production hosts; external unauthenticated scans run monthly; container images scanned on CI per-build with a weekly aggregation report; third-party dependency scans (SCA) run weekly for services and quarterly for partner libraries.
- CVE SLA matrix (attached cve-sla-matrix-2027-05.pdf): Critical = 7 days (investigate + mitigation/fix or compensating control), High = 30 days, Medium = 90 days, Low = discretionary maintenance queue. We escalate Critical to on-call and CISO pager.
- Evidence index (attached vm_scan_index_2027-05-01.csv) contains last three months for both internal and external scans with top finding summary.
- Example ticket: we included a redacted remediation ticket in Drive (link below) showing triage -> fix -> verification within 6 days for a recent critical kernel CVE in a dedicated pool.

Notes/Exceptions:
- For vendors where we do not have agent access we rely on attestation + quarterly SCA scans; those exceptions are documented in the index under 'scope_exceptions'.
- For third-party SaaS (managed DBs, 3rd party telemetry) we provide contracts/attestations rather than internal scans; we call those out in the packet.

Attachments: vm_scan_index_2027-05-01.csv, cve-sla-matrix-2027-05.pdf, scan-rhythm-summary-2027Q2.md
Drive packet: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B-VM-EVIDENCE (contains redacted ticket and screenshots)
HubSpot ref: HSB-98762

Will follow up with Karthik to add a short operations statement for the 'investigate' step.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Sr. Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@brightgate-audit.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 08:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request - VM evidence & SLA mapping for Aurora Payments SIG review

Samantha / team — adding operational detail for the packet. Please see the short runbook excerpt below (also in scan-rhythm-summary-2027Q2.md).

Runbook excerpt:
1) Detection & Triage (0–8 hrs for Critical): Automated alert from the scanner or telemetry into Jira (project: SEC-Remed). Pager duty notifies on-call. Triage includes reproducibility, blast-radius assessment, asset ownership assignment.
2) Containment / Mitigation (0–72 hrs for Critical): If a hotfix is available we apply to a canary subset; otherwise we implement network ACL or access restrictions as compensating control and schedule patch.
3) Remediation & Validation (target within SLA): Remediation performed in staging -> canary -> rollout. Validation includes re-scan and manual verification. Closure requires evidence in the ticket (patch diff, re-scan report).

We will include one redacted ticket export showing the timestamps for each step (the Drive link has it). For completeness — our continuous container scanning tool seeds the vulnerability database daily and we run a weekly policy job that auto-creates high-severity tickets in SEC-Remed.

If BrightGate needs a signed attestation for the SLA mapping we can provide an executive sign-off PDF; let us know the preferred signer.

- Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@brightgate-audit.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Murray <alex.murray@aurorapayments.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request - VM evidence & SLA mapping for Aurora Payments SIG review

Thanks Priya and Karthik — packet received and the summary is helpful. A couple of quick clarifications before we close the loop:

1) In the CSV index can you add a column for 'scan_auth_method' (agent / unauth / api) and one for 'scope_exceptions' (yes/no + short note)?
2) For the vendor-attested systems, please include the latest attestation date and contact (a single line in the CSV is fine).

If you can push a revised CSV by EOD PDT tomorrow we should be able to include it in Aurora's SIG response. Otherwise the rest looks good and we may request the executive attestation PDF (signed) for the SLA matrix.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Samantha
